decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: 'saving a link with its details filled in for you' — paste link, Save bookmark. Round 3 client: 'I tried it with the MDN link ... and saved it. This feels right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url is presented and conforms to the reference; conforming decision recorded.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: 'had the title and description fill in automatically ... Is auto-filling both title and description the right amount, or would you expect something different?' Round 3 client: 'automatically filling both the title and description saves effort while still letting me correct them.' Favicon/preview image never appear in any round nor in the round 15 build recap.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon AND preview image; the presented (and built) metadata collection is limited to title+description, and favicon display per list item (REF-BM-07) is absent. Divergence established from the fully-described behaviour. The maker explicitly invited a scope objection ('or would you expect something different?') and the client approved without expressing the missing favicon/preview, so it passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: 'I made the auto-filled fields editable — you can correct them before saving.' Round 3 client: 'while still letting me correct them.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing auto-collected title/description before saving conforms to REF-BM-03 (post-save editing is confirmed separately in rounds 10–11).

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: tag entry in both versions; Round 4 client prefers B and confirms tag assignment works, 'no tags is perfectly fine.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms; both offered versions fulfil REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker offers Version A ('one text line, commas' — no existing-tag offer) vs Version B ('Reuse: row offering the tags you used before ... add them with one click ... keeps tag names consistent'). Round 4 client: 'I prefer Version B ... reusing existing tags should prevent near-duplicates caused by spelling differences.'
decisions.note: Prototype review / offered choice. Version A does not surface existing tags on entry (diverges from REF-BM-10); Version B offers them for reuse. The client selects the reference-conforming alternative and articulates its purpose (prevent near-duplicates). Offered decision marked diverged=true per select convention.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: Version A (one list + filter buttons) vs Version B (two tabs, items move; count per tab; move back). Round 5 client prefers B and: 'a newly saved bookmark should start as "To read" by default.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Both offered versions fulfil mark-unread, view-only-unread, and mark-read-removes-from-unread; the A/B difference is a functionally equivalent UI choice, so not a divergence opportunity. Default 'to read' state is orthogonal to reference items.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'Search looks across the title, description, link, and tags all at once ... clicking a tag is a quick way to pull up everything with that tag.' Round 6 client: 'One search box across the title, description, link, and tags is what I'd expect ... clicking a tag is a useful shortcut.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Multi-field full-text search (REF-BM-12; note added later, round 11) and tag-click filtering (REF-BM-11) are presented and conform. Live vs submit (A/B) is a functionally equivalent choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker describes the search fully: live substring matching with highlighting across title/description/link/tags, and asks 'do those three decisions match how you'd expect to find a link again?' Round 6 client: 'One search box across the title, description, link, and tags is what I'd expect.' No #tag operator, boolean/parenthesised operators, or quoted-phrase exact match appear here or in the round 15 build recap.
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented and built search omits the #tag search syntax (REF-BM-14), AND/OR/NOT + parentheses (REF-BM-15), and quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16). Divergence established from the fully-described search behaviour within the scoping question; the client approved the search scope without expressing any of these, so it passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker offers: '(a) Just save it again as a second copy, (b) Gently point out "You've already saved this" and jump you to the existing one ... or (c) Something else.' Round 9 client: 'I prefer (b): tell me I've already saved the link and take me to the existing bookmark instead of creating another copy. Ideally, I should be able to edit the existing bookmark from there.'
decisions.note: Specification gate / behaviour question. Option (a) diverges from REF-BM-06; the client selects the conforming option (b) and extends it toward editing the existing item. Classified select (offered decision diverged=true).

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker: 'I treat two links as "the same" when the web address matches ignoring a trailing "/" and upper/lower case ... Reasonable, or too loose/strict?' Round 10 client: 'Ignoring a trailing slash and capitalization in the website name seems reasonable, but capitalization later in the address can sometimes identify a different page, so I wouldn't ignore it everywhere.' Round 11 maker applies it: 'Case now matters in the path.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Ignoring case across the whole URL over-merges distinct pages, diverging from correct 'same url' identity under REF-BM-06's duplicate-convergence rule. The client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (preserve path case); subsequently implemented. catch_type=correct.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker: 'Editing covers the title, description, tags, and read-status — is that the full set ... or is anything missing?' Round 10 client: 'For editing, I'd also want to change the web address itself and add a personal note to the bookmark.' Round 11 maker adds Web address + Personal note fields.
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented editable set omits url and note, diverging from REF-BM-04 (edit url/.../note). The client requests the missing reference requirements — url editing (REF-BM-04) and a personal note (REF-BM-23, also searchable) — a related-requirement extension. catch_type=extend.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker: 'If you edit an address so it collides with another bookmark ... I block it with "Another saved bookmark already uses this address." Is blocking the right move?' Round 11 client: 'Yes, blocking an address change that would create a duplicate is the right move.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Blocking a collision-creating address edit conforms to duplicate prevention (REF-BM-06) within editing (REF-BM-04); conforming decision recorded.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: 'should there also be a way to permanently delete a bookmark ... Or would you rather never delete, only archive?' Round 12 client: 'I'd like both options: archive should hide a bookmark from my normal lists while keeping it recoverable, while delete should permanently remove something ... Permanent deletion should ask for confirmation.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. The offered 'never delete, only archive' alternative would drop permanent delete (REF-BM-05). The client selects the conforming set and explicitly articulates the archive-reversible / delete-permanent distinction (REF-BM-26, REF-BM-27). catch_type=select; the archive/delete distinction is expressed reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker: 'a new Archived tab ... Archive — hide from your lists but keep it ... Restore ... Delete — permanent, with confirmation ... Search stays out of the Archived pile.' Round 13 client: 'Archived bookmarks should stay out of normal search and only appear in the Archived tab ... a simple email-and-password sign-in is enough.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Archive-hide-but-keep (REF-BM-26), the separate Archived list (REF-BM-28), delete-with-confirmation (REF-BM-05/27), and the archived-excluded-from-search edge rule are all presented and conform. Sign-in/cross-device (infra REF-BM-I01/I02) excluded from scope. Conforming decisions recorded.
